title: Investigating Behavior Cloning from Few Demonstrations for Autonomous Driving based on Bird's-Eye View in Simulated Cities
abstract: arXiv:2610.20203v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This paper investigates the use of Behavior Cloning (BC) for autonomous driving from a bird's-eye view (BEV) perspective in simulated urban environments. BC uses supervised learning to mimic expert driving behaviors. Previous works have applied BC in the CARLA simulator but did not fully address the challenges of traffic light compliance. Our approach enhances BC by integrating a kernel density estimator to adjust training sample weights based on action density, thereby improving the learning of rare but critical actions such as stopping at red lights and accelerating at green lights, specially in scenarios of scarce number of expert demonstrations. Using BEV inputs, which provide an abstract top-down view of the driving environment, our method simplifies the policy learning process. The trained convolutional neural network (CNN) outputs steering and acceleration actions based on these BEV inputs and additional state variables. Experim

translated_title: 探究在模拟城市中基于鸟瞰图、从少量演示数据中进行行为克隆的自动驾驶方法
translated_abstract: 本文研究了在模拟城市环境中，从鸟瞰图（BEV）视角使用行为克隆（BC）实现自动驾驶的方法。行为克隆通过监督学习来模仿专家的驾驶行为。以往的研究已在CARLA模拟器中应用了行为克隆，但未能充分解决遵守交通信号灯这一挑战。我们的方法通过引入核密度估计器对行为克隆进行改进，根据动作密度调整训练样本的权重，从而改善了对罕见但关键动作（如红灯停车、绿灯起步加速）的学习，尤其是在专家演示数据稀缺的场景下。鸟瞰图输入提供了驾驶环境的抽象俯视视图，利用这种输入，我们的方法简化了策略学习过程。训练好的卷积神经网络（CNN）基于这些鸟瞰图输入和额外的状态变量输出转向与加速动作。实验……
tldr: 该论文提出在行为克隆中引入核密度估计器，根据动作密度对训练样本加权，从而在专家演示稀缺的情况下，基于鸟瞰图输入显著提升自动驾驶对红灯停车等罕见但关键动作的学习能力。
en_tdlr: This paper enhances behavior cloning with a kernel density estimator that reweights training samples by action density, enabling better learning of rare but critical actions (e.g., traffic light compliance) from few expert demonstrations using bird's-eye view inputs.
